external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A person enrolled in the grocery loyalty programme.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: members' phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone running the mobile app and retaining its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

external_entities.name: partner server
external_entities.description: A server operated by another company that runs a partner app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to authenticate and access rewards.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles partner authorization, and issues tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The member's sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; nobody decided an idle timeout for it.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API used to access and change loyalty points and redeem gift cards.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It does not check which client or which audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application operated by another company that can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
processes.notes: Every partner app receives every scope.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: The member's browser used to sign in and return the authorization code.
processes.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application used to close a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member identities, credentials, authorization artifacts, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: The database also contains authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and closed-account status.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing member balances and points transactions.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: authorization code flow
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.

data_flows.name: keep refresh token
data_flows.description: The mobile app keeps a refresh token on the member's phone.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.
data_flows.notes: A mobile refresh token never expires; every use slides its expiry forward another ninety days.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The partner app uses a client ID and client secret; the secret is sent in the request body.
data_flows.data_description: client credentials, scopes, and token requests

data_flows.name: authorize member
data_flows.description: A partner app initiates member authorization through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page

data_flows.name: sign-in and consent
data_flows.description: The browser submits member sign-in and consent interactions to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen
data_flows.notes: The sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; no idle timeout was decided.

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with the registered URI.

data_flows.name: show member points
data_flows.description: A partner app accesses member points through the rewards API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.

data_flows.name: maintain identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes identity and authorization data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.data_description: accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read and write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: Redeeming points for a gift card requires a valid access token carrying the redeem scope.

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: obtain access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close member account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Closing an account does not affect that member's refresh tokens.

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud environment containing the authorization server, rewards API, support console, and stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing members' phones and the mobile app.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies that host partner apps.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal information, passwords, tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member-linked balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because it stores requests and headers, which can include credentials and member-related information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the API log store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
